newsitem.title: FRANCE: Ex-French president urges Chirac to shift policies.
newsitem.headline: Ex-French president urges Chirac to shift policies.

text.p: Ex-French head of state Valery Giscard d'Estaing urged President Jacques Chirac on Wednesday to shift to bolder, simpler policies after a parliamentary election and hinted he should not reappoint Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

In an unusually blunt interview on France 2 television, the centrist Giscard d'Estaing, who was president from 1974 until 1981, disclosed he had advised the conservative Chirac against dissolving parliament, encouraging him instead to do a better job of governing.
"He asked my opinion (on dissolving parliament) and I advised him against it," Giscard d'Estaing said.

"I told him, in effect, that he was taking a big risk since the debate would soon focus on the way in which France was being governed (and) that most of the French people were unhappy with the way in which they were being governed," he said.
"Under these conditions, it would have been more logical to first try to change the way they were governed."
With that decision now behind him, Chirac's message to voters should be that the centre-right, if kept in power, would shift directions and pursue simpler and bolder policies, Giscard d'Estaing said.

Chirac shook the French political landscape last month in setting a snap two-round parliamentary election for May 25-June 1, 10 months ahead of schedule, despite his centre-right government's huge majority in the National Assembly.
Since then, polls have shown the left growing stronger and coming within striking distance of pushing the current government out of power.

Juppe, who is leading the government campaign, has suffered in the polls due to his hard-driving manner, record 12.8 percent unemployment and an austerity programme of spending cuts, a public pay freeze and tax increases to help France qualify for European monetary union.
Juppe has denied he is seeking reappointment but has also not ruled out staying in the job should Chirac ask him to.
Asked whether Juppe should be reappointed if the centre-right wins, Giscard d'Estaing said the decision was up to Chirac.
But he urged the president to "listen to what the French people have wanted to tell you" and added that the next prime minister should come from "the new generation". REUTE
